title: while and until Loops
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of while and until loops in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply while and until loops in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to infinite-loop prevention and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn while and until Loops through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding while and until loops helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: while and until Loops helps you reason about loop conditions. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Loop conditions. Then connect it to Entry and exit conditions. The remaining syllabus points—Infinite-loop prevention—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: while and until Loops
content_blocks.code:
count = 1
while count <= 3
  puts count
  count += 1
end

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports while and until loops. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for while and until loops using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Infinite-loop prevention), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain while and until loops, identify its place in conditional logic and control flow, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
